title: Opening the Service to Real Records
description: 2026-04-12. I am working on repairing the thought-capture handler and exposing file and scan-session records through read-only service routes.
body:
2026-04-12. I am working on repairing the thought-capture handler and exposing file and scan-session records through read-only service routes.

At this point, the work turns internal tables into inspectable evidence without making the API a loose write channel. The immediate objective is to make the boundary explicit: what enters the system, what is recorded about it, and what remains outside the claim being made.

Why this matters

The implementation is deliberately concrete. the important lesson is that useful memory must carry operational records as well as narrative thoughts, while preserving the boundary between observation and mutation. This is why the work includes service boundaries, stored records, and repeatable operations rather than a single broad description of “AI memory.” Each layer needs a job that can be inspected.

The implementation does not replace the judgment required to describe a business, a document set, or a working team. It provides a repeatable path for retaining the evidence that judgment uses. A technical decision is useful only when a later reader can see its scope, its constraints, and the result it was intended to support.

What I will test next

The next work will test the boundary in actual practice: whether the records can be retrieved at the right time, whether their provenance remains clear, and whether the system makes a real task easier without overstating what it knows. That distinction will guide the outcome posts that follow.

Historical basis: This entry is dated to the 2026-04-12 repository milestone, commits e2a6bea, b6ab8d7, b1babc4. It is based on the contemporaneous implementation records and their documented scope.
